reader_question: How does homeownership differ by age, and has that changed?
title: Householders under 35 were the least likely of five age groups to own their homes in each year shown, 1995 to 2025.
reading_guide: Each panel draws one age group in ink over the other four in gray, on one shared scale.
measure_line: Share of households that own their home, by the householder’s age, every fifth year from 1995 to 2025, three decades, United States
source_line: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Current Population Survey/Housing Vacancy Survey, Annual Statistics 2025, Table 17, homeownership rate by age of householder, 1982 to 2025, United States. Retrieved November 11, 2026. Survey estimates; the 2025 average leaves out October, when no data were collected.
alt: Five small panels of homeownership by age from 1995 to 2025, one group in ink in each: under 35 lowest, near 37 percent in 2025; 65 and over highest, near 79 percent.

table.caption: Share of households that own their home, by age of householder, percent

notes_internal: Rule 14.8's correct plate. Checked by script: under 35 lowest by more than 15 points every year.
